title: Category
description: Optional display metadata for a category folder, in a `_category.json` sidecar. Overrides the folder-name-derived title (which can't punctuate or translate) and can add a per-language name and an icon. See docs/archive/PLANNING.md §4.

title.description: Display name, in the same shape as a topic's title or a word entry: a plain string where the name is global ("Film & TV"), a language map where it translates, or a short/long pair — `short` on the row, `long` in a hover. Falls back to the title-cased folder name.

order.description: Where this sits among its siblings, lowest first. Undeclared sorts last, alphabetically — so ordering a few of them needs nothing on the rest. The tree is otherwise the file system's, which puts Animation first and Gaming sixth for no reason anyone chose.

hideRulersByDefault.description: When true, the fame rulers of this category's topics start hidden behind a single toggle on the category row rather than shown. Declaring the field (either value) makes this category an independent ruler-visibility boundary: its toggle governs its subtree down to the next node that declares the field, and children without the field inherit this value.

sharedEnglishToggle.description: When true, this category's row carries one toggle switching every list below it to its English entries at once — for a category whose topics are variations of a single list (the nine Pokémon generations), where making the choice nine times is the same choice. The per-topic toggles stay available underneath. Governs down to the next category that declares the field.

langMapString.description: A per-language string: keys are language codes ("en" is the required base), values the localized text. Languages that match "en" are omitted.

locString.description: A string that is the same everywhere (plain string) or translates (language map).

namePair.description: A short (row) and long (hover) form of the name; each may itself be a language map when only that part translates.

word.description: Mirrors `word` in topic.schema.json, so a category's title has the same shape as a topic's. Repeated rather than referenced across files: the two schemas are loaded independently.
